paper_title: Mixed molecular orientations promote charge transport in bulk heterojunction solar cells

knowledge_points.content: A mixed texture of face-on and edge-on molecular orientations can be more beneficial for out-of-plane charge transport in bulk heterojunctions than a predominantly face-on orientation.
knowledge_points.evidence: By systematically varying the molecular orientation of poly(3-hexylthiophene-2,5-diyl) (P3HT) in P3HT:fullerene bulk heterojunctions, we show that a mixed face-on and edge-on texture can be beneficial for out-of-plane charge flow.

knowledge_points.content: In bulk heterojunctions, lateral charge transport pathways provided by edge-on molecular stacking allow charges to circumvent excluded volumes, such as acceptor domains that block hole transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: Lateral pathways provided by an edge-on orientation can promote three-dimensional charge flow by helping holes circumvent acceptor domains in which hole transport is excluded.

knowledge_points.content: In P3HT:PC61BM BHJ films, an edge-on to face-on ratio of 4.4 (achieved by annealing at 195 °C) resulted in a 31% higher out-of-plane hole current compared to films with a ratio of 1.5.
knowledge_points.evidence: Instead, an edge-on to face-on ratio of 4.4 (annealed at 195 °C) led to a 31% higher out-of-plane hole current compared to films with an edge-on to face-on ratio of 1.5 (annealed at 100 °C).

knowledge_points.content: Increasing the annealing temperature of P3HT:PC61BM films from 100 °C to 220 °C shifts the P3HT population from a mixed texture (44% edge-on) to a predominantly edge-on orientation (95% edge-on).
knowledge_points.evidence: As shown in Fig. 1(c), as the annealing temperature is increased, the P3HT molecules within the film increasingly favor an edge-on orientation, with the edge-on proportion growing from 44% to 95% over the measured annealing range.

knowledge_points.content: The effective lateral current spreading area (Aeff) in a vertical device geometry can be quantified using conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM) by comparing currents through a bare film (Ip) and through a microelectrode of known area (Am).
knowledge_points.evidence: The effective current spreading area Aeff during C-AFM can be obtained from Aeff = (Ip/Im)Am where Am is the microelectrode area.

knowledge_points.content: To accurately quantify oriented molecular populations from GIWAXS data, the scattering intensity along the azimuthal angle (χ) must be corrected by multiplying the integrated intensity by sin(χ) to account for the three-dimensional reciprocal space.
knowledge_points.evidence: To quantify the oriented populations over the full reciprocal space, the scattering intensity along the azimuthal angle (χ) was adjusted by multiplying the integrated intensity by sin(χ).

knowledge_points.content: P3HT in P3HT:PC61BM blends exhibits a melting point between 200 °C and 205 °C, characterized by a sharp increase in total crystallinity due to heterogeneous nucleation during cooling.
knowledge_points.evidence: The melting point of P3HT in the P3HT:PC61BM blends can be identified by the sudden increase in total crystallinity, between 200 °C and 205 °C.

knowledge_points.content: The lateral current spreading radius in P3HT:PC61BM films correlates strongly with the edge-on to face-on molecular ratio, with a coefficient of determination of 0.967.
knowledge_points.evidence: The current spreading radius closely correlates with the edge-on to face-on ratio, with a coefficient of determination of 0.967.

knowledge_points.content: In GIWAXS patterns for P3HT, the (100) lamellar peak appears at q ≈ 0.38 Å⁻¹ and the (010) π-π stacking peak appears at q ≈ 1.6 Å⁻¹.
knowledge_points.evidence: Edge-on P3HT stacking is evident from the distinct (100) lamellar peak at qz = 0.38 Å⁻¹... and an in-plane π-π stacking (010) peak at qx = 1.6 Å⁻¹.

knowledge_points.content: The improvement in hole transport for P3HT:PC61BM films annealed between 100 °C and 195 °C is attributed to changes in molecular orientation rather than increased crystallinity, as the total crystallite population slightly decreases in this range.
knowledge_points.evidence: For films annealed up to 200 °C we observed a slight drop in the total P3HT crystallite population; therefore, the improvement in hole transport between 100 °C to 195 °C cannot be attributed to an increase in crystallinity.
